$comment: Which anchor on /spec/ renders which section of IAES_SPEC.md.
/spec/ is a WEB RENDERING of the specification, not a second authority. It
is written by hand, and it silently fell two releases behind: when 2.0 was
published the page still rendered 1.3 and was missing six whole sections,
including References -- which another page of this site had just started
citing as the place where the specification governs.
tools/check_spec_sections.py reads this and requires, for every '## ' in the
specification at the tag SERVED.json names, an anchor that exists on the
page. It checks PRESENCE BY ANCHOR, deliberately, not by heading text: the
title 'Severity Levels' became 'Severity Standard' in a release, and a guard
keyed to the visible title would have fired on a correct rename. A guard
that fires on correct content is a guard that gets switched off.
It does not check that the rendered prose matches. That would need a
generator, which is a different project. This closes the failure that
actually happened: losing an entire section of a release without anyone

page_only.$comment: Anchors the page carries that the specification has no section for. Version History renders the specification's version table, which lives inside the document rather than under its own '## '.
page_only.version-history: renders the specification's version history table
